title: Timed push fights wip snapshots; benign non-FF reads like a lost origin
description:
While a durable local run's snapshots hold the attempt branch, the supervisor's timed push of HEAD is refused as non-fast-forward every half-interval (push.last is not advanced on push_failed), so a clean run logs 'the timed push of <branch> failed' for its whole life — the same log line a genuinely unreachable origin produces. The snapshots are the durability mechanism during a run, so the push is correctly refused; what is missing is the distinction. A small tick could let pushBranch recognise 'origin holds this attempt's own wip snapshot' (the checkout's ticfac-wip-pushed record names it) and read it as up-to-date, leaving real failures visible.
evidence: internal/exec/subprocess/supervisor.go maybePush (push.last unchanged on push_failed) and pushBranch's non-FF refusal; harness/src/workspace/checkpoints.ts pushWipCheckpoint writes the ticfac-wip-pushed record
